title: Rosalind and the Gravity
premise: On the orbital colony of Meridian Station, Odile Kavanagh smuggles forbidden memories in her own head while tending the beacon that keeps the colony invisible to both warring fleets. When the station's children begin dreaming the same dream — a message encoded in the beacon's original architect, who turns out to be Odile's erased first love — she realizes the war's truce was built on a lie the beacon was designed to expose. Hunted by customs, the fleet, and her own crumbling cover identity, Odile must decide whether to broadcast the truth and shatter the fragile peace, or let the beacon die and the war resume. In the end, the children themselves carry the message through the blockade, and the truth ends the war at the cost of Odile's memories of everyone she loves — except the one she rebuilt them for.
about_author: Xanthe Okonkwo is the pen name of a former radio astronomer who left academia after a decade of listening to signals nobody claimed to have sent. Their fiction has appeared in three languages and one very confused anthology of maritime poetry.

chapters.title: Contraband Heartbeats
chapters.summary: Odile smuggles a widow's memory of her dead son past orbital customs, hiding it inside her own recollections of a lighthouse she's never seen. POV: Odile. Establishes her double life — memory-runner and anonymous beacon keeper — and the quiet ache of carrying other people's most precious moments while owning almost none of her own.

chapters.title: The Children Who Dream in Unison
chapters.summary: Forty-seven children across Meridian Station wake from the identical dream: a woman's voice counting down from a number no adult recognizes. Customs officer Bren Okafor, Odile's sometime lover, opens an investigation into 'contagious cognition.' POV: alternating Odile and Bren. The station's fragile anonymity begins to crack.

chapters.title: What the Beacon Remembers
chapters.summary: Odile descends into the beacon's maintenance shaft and finds the architecture is a memory-palace — someone encoded a full human mind into its lattice. The voice in the children's dream is that mind, degrading. POV: Odile. She realizes the beacon was commissioned by someone who loved her enough to be forgotten by her.

chapters.title: Truce Expiry
chapters.summary: The fleet announces the ceasefire expires in nineteen days. Bren discovers Odile's smuggling route and confronts her — not with arrest, but with a choice: help him trace the dream, or lose him. POV: Bren. His loyalty to duty wars with his loyalty to her, and duty is losing.

chapters.title: Found Family, Assembled Illegally
chapters.summary: Odile's crew — a defrocked teacher, a customs-deserter, and the dreamer children's ringleader, ten-year-old Sefu — gather in the beacon shaft. The encoded mind, calling itself Rosalind, begins speaking through the children. POV: Sefu. The crew becomes a family around a ghost.

chapters.title: The Message in the War
chapters.summary: Rosalind's fragmented memory reveals she was the truce's secret architect: the ceasefire isn't diplomacy, it's a countdown to her message being decoded. Both fleets have agents on-station hunting the beacon. POV: Odile. She understands that invisibility was never safety — it was a cage someone built around a truth.

chapters.title: Customs Raid
chapters.summary: Fleet agents storm Meridian, and Bren must choose publicly between his commission and the family in the shaft. He burns his career to buy them hours, and is taken. POV: Bren. The cost of love against duty comes due, and he pays it without regret.

chapters.title: Nineteen Days, Spent
chapters.summary: With hours left, Rosalind offers Odile a terrible trade: the message can only be carried by a mind with room for it, and Odile's smuggled memories must be spent as fuel. POV: Odile. She begins surrendering her own past — every client's memory, every stolen joy — to complete the transmission.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: The children, immune to fleet scanners because they dream rather than remember, carry Rosalind's completed message to the beacon's transmitter during the fleet's final assault. The truth of the war's manufactured origin floods both fleets' channels. POV: Sefu. Climax — the message lands, and the war stops mid-breath.

chapters.title: Gravity, and What Holds
chapters.summary: The war ends; the truce becomes a treaty built on the broadcast truth. Odile, memory-stripped to near-blankness, wakes to a found family who refuses to let her stay a stranger — Sefu reads her Rosalind's last letter, and love begins the slow work of re-remembering. POV: Odile. Resolution: some gravity you choose.
